description: A palm of floodplain (varzea), riverbank, swamp, terra firme, 12-20 m tall. A cone of roots shows at the stem base: roots bright red when young, up to 1 m long (cone height not given; 1 m is the root length). 5-10(-20) leaves, spreading and somewhat arched, with pendulous pinnae. Fruit: globose drupe, 0.9-1.3 cm, purple-black epicarp, thin pulp; more than 1,000 fruits per bunch.

notes: Template palm: a palm: Corner's model (one unbranched stem, a crown of large leaves at its top), the palm block from the research's. Crown width: twice the frond length, the fronds arching (no source gives the crown's width). Leaf size clamped to 0.6 m (the source's 74 cm is past what a leaf card carries). NOT SOURCED (the template's or a default value): leaf colour (a tropical evergreen's mid green); the stem's diameter at the top (0.85 of the base's); stilt root count (8-16); stilt root thickness (3 cm); the stilt roots' angle (20 degrees off the vertical). Research notes: Height and diameter are the species range (Henderson & Galeano 1996); adults reach about 20 m and 16 cm at breast height (da Rocha et al. 2025). Leaves: 5-10(-20) in the monograph; 10-15 in Spanish/Portuguese Wikipedia; about 14 in adults (da Rocha). leaf.length_cm is the rachis (1.6-3.6 m); the petiole adds (0-)12-57 cm. Habitat: var. precatoria lowland rain forest, commonly along rivers in periodically inundated areas, below 350 m (occasionally to 600 m). da Rocha lists terra firme, swampy blackwater lowlands (baixios) and high varzea. UTP says 'swampy ground'. Phenology: no Madre de Dios data. fruiting_months are from the upper Acre River (Epitaciolandia, Acre, Brazil, next to Madre de Dios): baixio Mar-Jun, terra firme Jun-Oct. Elsewhere in Acre: Chico Mendes reserve Mar-Sep; Tarauaca baixio Jan-Apr, terra firme Jul-Sep. Inflorescences emerge mainly Aug-Dec at Manaus (central Amazon), so flowering_months are left empty. Flower colour not found. Eaten_by: da Rocha says the fruits feed birds, fruit bats and rodents but names no species; no species-level frugivore source found (toucan/guan studies found were on Euterpe edulis). Evergreen is assumed for a palm, not stated.
